rules: Sand is MANDATORY for any start on a wet rail on grade or on curves < R100 (sanders lead axle each direction; mu_sand 0.25)
L4.1: NO flow divider - every start is an equal-torque (parallel-loop) start: cap = 4 x mu x lightest axle; electronic traction control (pump destroke on slip, auto-sand) keeps adhesion; start in 1st

Front: Loco Bot shell package (S17 ledger) +2431 kg on the front truck + 151 kg pocket ballast plates + 68.2 kg BT-1 battery (F2 +12.7 kN) - equal-torque 2% start needs 0 kg pocket ballast for margin 1.0, 0 kg for 1.10 (1.5 t pockets) - plates set by the 1.10 rule (2 minimum)
start.note: L4.1 GOVERNING cap = equal-torque (parallel loop) 4*mu*lightest axle (Stress Bot t1). The *_divider_* columns are kept for information only (L4 gear divider deleted). TE at 350 bar exceeds the dry cap -> adhesion-limited.

speed.stop_rule: L4.2: stroke stop 42 cc sealed + HARD tamper-sealed 2,600 rpm engine limit (no high idle above rated): 5.96 mph loaded in 2nd; no-load 6.47 mph (eta_v 0.99); 7 mph trip independent
speed.spin_note: L4.2: MS05 2-speed valves re-wired FAIL-TO-1st (de-energized = 468 cc); the 2nd-gear coil is fed THROUGH a hard-wired PNOZ s30 speed-threshold contact (closed only >= 1.5 mph ground speed) in series with PLUS+1 (2nd commanded >= 3.0 mph with pony/axle agreement). A single axle can spin in 2nd only while the other 3 roll at >= 1.5 mph -> 377 rpm vs 430 (util 0.88); at standstill or on any coil/wire/24 V failure the motors are in 1st -> 228 rpm vs 370 (util 0.62). The no-interlock standstill-in-2nd figure (457 rpm, util 1.06) needs PLUS+1 AND the s30 contact to fail together. Per-motor electronic overspeed destroke at 420 rpm (PLUS+1) is a further layer.
speed.hardware_note: With the stroke stop removed the hardware tops out at 7.6 mph (2nd) - far below L3's 10 mph capability
speed.shift: PLUS+1 shifts all 4 motors together: 1st (468 cc) below 2.5 mph or loop dp > 300 bar; 2nd (234 cc) above 3.0 mph with dp < 180 bar (hysteresis). Shift-on-the-move rating AWAIT Poclain.

power_speed.method: pump allowance x pump 0.855 x motor 0.92 hm x 0.95 vol x dp/(dp+10) x chain 0.97; best of 1st/2nd displacement with dp <= 350; flow cap at the 42 cc stop; 6 mph governor

hotday.rule: compressor electric clutch engages only at low traction demand or MR < 7.0 bar; anti-stall map drops to 34.5 kW while clutched; hydraulic cooler fan electric 24 V from the genset charger (not on the engine/alternator)
hotday.cooler_spec: Air-oil cooler >= 14 kW at 43 °C OUTSIDE air, oil in 70 °C (ETD 27 K), on the low-pressure return / flushing line, own ducted louvre on the tender LEFT wall X3455-4145 (Tender Bot TB-2), case-pressure bypass check upstream; AWAIT supplier curve

chain.vertical_travel_note: motor on the sprung truck frame, chain line horizontal: 25 mm primary travel changes centres by 0.7 mm
chain.reversing: bidirectional + motor brake through the chain: both strands become tight in turn -> fixed centres (slotted motor bracket + jack screws), NO spring idler
maintenance: Oil bath ISO VG 220 EP: check level weekly (sight glass), change every 500 h or each season (magnetic drain plug)

Tension: check sag monthly / 100 h at static ride height: 17-20 mm at mid-span (keeps >= 14 mm at full suspension travel) with the motor brake released; adjust with the motor-bracket jack screws and re-torque the slide bolts
Elongation: measure over 10 pitches every 250 h; REPLACE the chain at 2 % (short 11-pitch centres wear sprockets fast); 3 % is the absolute limit (slide range is sized for it)

Sprockets: replace the 15T at every chain change. The 45T is a rim-only SPLIT ring (2 halves, Source Bot rev 3) bolted to the pressed-hub flange: unbolt and replace in place, NO pressing and NO wheelset drop
Seal plate / breather: inspect for leaks weekly; oil on the wheel or rail = stop the train (adhesion)

MBL_L42.rule: SPEC: ANSI 120-2 chain with a mill certificate of breaking strength >= 326 kN per lot (same factor at 430 bar). Standard Tsubaki RS120-2 (296 kN published) is NOT accepted unless the PE accepts SF 8.41 on ultimate at the 430 bar spike; a higher-strength 120-2 (e.g. heavy/super series) certified >= 326 kN is a VENDOR-BATCH item (no contact without the owner)

take_up.sense: any vertical axle movement from the horizontal static chain line LENGTHENS the centres (C' = sqrt(C^2 + dz^2))
take_up.verdict: OK WITHOUT AN IDLER: set the sag at static ride height to 17-20 mm (motor brake released, axle at ride height); at full bump/rebound it falls to ~14 mm (>= 2% of span), never tight. Slotted motor mount (4 x M20 10.9 in 50 mm slots) + 2 x M20 jack screws, slide 37 mm covers 3 % wear.

rules: Hard vertical bump stops +/-22 mm axle vs truck frame (primary travel 25 kept as the case/seal-plate envelope)

RE-SHIM PROCEDURE: restore body/coupler height for wheel wear with shims at the CENTRE PLATE / side bearers (body-truck), NEVER under the primary springs. A primary re-shim (spring set) is limited to 3 mm total and is ALWAYS followed by a motor-slide reset: loosen the 4 x M20, re-set the sag to 17-20 mm at ride height with the chain line horizontal +/-3 mm, re-torque 610 N.m, record
Sag 17-20 mm at static ride height, checked monthly / 100 h; chain replaced at 2 % elongation (HARD limit; 3 % no longer allowed)
Oil level: lower strand immersed 20-25 mm static (was 6-12) so the lead axle stays immersed when it lifts on a climb; or a slinger (CWF option)
chain_slack_L41.verdict: PASS: with the corrected geometry the slack lasts to 30.8 mm of bump at sag 17 (chain line horizontal) vs the 22 mm stop (margin 1.40); 28.0 mm with a 3 mm primary shim. A 10 mm primary re-shim without a motor reset would give 22.4 mm - NOT permitted by the procedure.

wheel_wear_L41.verdict: Ø1430 ADOPTED as the driver CONDEMNING DIAMETER (after re-profiling); FLANGE: withdraw at 28 mm, re-profile to <= 27 mm (train-wide, L4.2; replaces the L4.1 30 mm limit); reverse full-train start limit 1.20 %.

T04_release_L41.principle: NO 4th dry-break, all on the loco: release pressure is taken from the loco's own hydrostatic loop. Loss of loop or charge pressure APPLIES the T04 (purely hydraulic, no electronics needed); the accumulator serves ONLY the guarded manual release.
T04_release_L41.superseded_by: L42.T04_charge_feed (L4.2: loop shuttle DELETED, T04 fed from the H1 charge circuit M3 port)
circuit: 1 [L4.1, SUPERSEDED] LP-select shuttle across loop A/B (hot-oil shuttle type, spring-centred, body >= 450 bar, 10-size cartridge or equal) -> picks the low side = charge pressure (22-28 bar running)
2 Pressure filter 10 um with bypass indicator (loop oil into the brake circuit)

3 3-way pressure-REDUCING/RELIEVING cartridge, set 20 bar (range 7-35, inlet >= 450 bar rated); with the inlet below setting it is fully open, so the brake line FOLLOWS a falling charge pressure -> brakes apply on loss of loop/charge
4 3/2 solenoid poppet, 24 V DC, NORMALLY VENTED (de-energized = brake port to case drain = APPLY); PLUS+1 energizes to release

5 Fixed choke Ø2.4 mm (ASSUMED until Poclain gives the T04 release volume) in the common brake line + 1.0 L diaphragm DAMPING accumulator (pre-charge 13.5 bar) on the brake side: every apply path (solenoid vent or supply loss) passes the choke -> delay 1.0 s, rise 3.0 s (required >= 1.0 / >= 2.0 s for the run-in result); release in ~4.8 s
6 Brake-line ball shuttle (high select) feeding the 4 T04 ports from EITHER the service line (5) OR the manual-release line (7); the unused inlet is vented

7 MANUAL RELEASE branch: check valve from the reducing-valve inlet -> 6.0 L bladder accumulator (210 bar class, pre-charge 13.5 bar, safety block with isolation, bleed and gauge) + hand pump 12 cm3/stroke with check (dead-loco recharge) -> guarded 3/2 manual valve (normally vented, padlock, limit switch to PLUS+1 = traction inhibit + BP stays vented) -> shuttle 6
8 Charge pressure switch, 17 bar falling, hard-wired with the T04-line switch: vents the BP FIRST (train air brakes lead), then the choked T04 follows
9 Last resort: T04 mechanical release screws (M12, per Poclain) for rescue towing
failure_modes: Engine stall / loop loss at speed: charge decays -> switch vents BP -> T04 applies through the choke (dynamic use logged; inspect per Poclain after each; 10 dynamic uses max)
24 V loss: solenoid vents -> choked apply; BP vents (ASCO de-energize-to-vent)
Hose burst on the brake line: brake applies (spring)
Manual valve left open: limit switch inhibits traction and holds the BP vented; accumulator volume only lasts 2 releases
T04_release_L41.supersedes: L4.1 loco_valves 0.75 L accumulator ON the brake line (it held release ~30 s after a stall) - REMOVED to meet 'loss of loop/charge applies the brake'
T04_release_L41.held: Poclain: T04 release volume, full-release pressure, choke size (vendor ask HELD - no contact)

pressure_L42.basis: L4.2 pressure revision (Source Bot: no -16 assembly rated >= 450 bar): PL 350 unchanged (working pull and gradeability unchanged), HPRV 380 (was 400) = the original Oct 27 basis, 30 bar PL-HPRV spacing
pressure_L42.loop_parts: Loop components rated >= 420 bar WP >= HPRV 380 (standard -16 hose, code 62 and 24 deg S25 ends at the maker's 420, Parker -16 whip restraint 420); the transient spike (~430 bar) is covered by the ISO 18752 / ISO 6605 impulse rating (133 % of WP); strength cases are checked at 430 bar
pressure_L42.danfoss: The Danfoss HPRV overshoot figure is INFORMATION ONLY (vendor batch), not gating
pressure_L42.rerun: All strength checks that used HPRV 400 re-run at the 430 bar STRENGTH basis (transient spike; HPRV 380 is the setting): spline, 45T ring bolts, hub fit, motor bearing radial, chain pull/MBL, motor bracket, axle seat, traction pin service case, safety-chain lugs. Run-in trip cases keep the Stress Bot 400 bar hydraulic force (conservative).

traction_pin.bearing: GE120ES-class spherical plain bearing, RADIAL load (re-selected from the GE100ES: the L4.1 pin carries longitudinal load only; T1-f 'vertical 273 kN' superseded); static radial rating >= 2 x 144 kN (AWAIT SKF data)
traction_pin.housing: PL20 housing ring welded to the transom web, 2 x 10 fillets all round (PE verify); pin engagement >= 60 mm over the full centre-plate shim range (0-12 mm)
traction_pin.clearance: pin Ø120 vs motor brackets 25-55 mm -> 15-45 mm after the +10 mm radius; vs MS05 60-80 mm (+22 at 2 % chain stretch) -> 50-70 / 28-48 mm: PASS (model.py now has the pin)

centre_plate.design: LAMINATED ELASTOMER centre pad (longitudinal shear stiffness <= 3.0 MN/m) with a PTFE-faced yaw slide (mu <= 0.08) on the flat-lined plate: the pad shears instead of sticking, so the stiff Ø120 pin carries the traction at 0.65 m; a rigid steel plate would put mu N at 1.11 m (sweep: rigid-plate margins)

sanding.layout: Sanders on BOTH powered trucks: nozzles ahead of the LEAD axle of EACH truck in EACH direction (forward F1 + R1, reverse F2 + R2) so the lightest axle (R1 forward, F2 reverse) is always sanded directly, PLUS a nozzle ahead of each trailing axle (so no axle relies on carry-over); 8 nozzles per truck, 2 boxes per truck
sanding.proof: Sand-box level switch per box + flow proof (air-pressure switch downstream of each sand valve, or a sand-flow sensor): a failed proof inhibits starts on grades >= 1 % and alarms
sanding.rule: Pre-sand on every start with the grade >= 1 % or a wet rail; sand is MANDATORY on wet rail
sanding.reverse_verdict: Reverse 2 % full-train start with sand on both trucks: margin 0.899 (< 1.10, NOT met - the lightest axle F2 is already sanded, so sand cannot add adhesion beyond mu 0.25). Grade for 1.10: 1.39 % new / 1.35 % worn (dry or sanded), 1.39 / 1.35 degraded carry-over ; the reverse pull cap of record 28.9 kN with the same 1.10 gives 1.21 % (GOVERNS) -> REVERSE FULL-TRAIN START LIMIT 1.20 % (all files)

K2a.rule: PLUS+1 caps the forward TE command at 33.0 kN (1.01 x the 2 % need) so no driver wheel exceeds 26 kN (K2-a); reverse pull is capped at 28.9 kN of record (adhesion cap 30.0; wheel 25.74 kN)

hill_hold.rule: Friction brakes (loco air calipers + train air) stay APPLIED on a start until loop dp >= p_hold(grade) + 20 bar and TE is established; then released. During any slip destroke PLUS+1 never reduces dp below p_hold for the measured grade (inclinometer); any reverse motion (pony quadrature direction) -> brakes apply + alarm
hill_hold.slip_sequence: slip detected -> sand -> destroke to v_ref x 1.05 but dp >= p_hold -> recover at 0.5 kN/s; if slip persists at p_hold for 3 s -> brakes apply, traction off (no roll-back)

A single axle can spin in 2nd only while the other 3 roll at >= 1.5 mph -> 377 rpm vs 430 (util 0.88); at standstill or on any coil/wire/24 V failure the motors are in 1st -> 228 rpm vs 370 (util 0.62). The no-interlock standstill-in-2nd figure (457 rpm, util 1.06) needs PLUS+1 AND the s30 contact to fail together. Per-motor electronic overspeed destroke at 420 rpm (PLUS+1) is a further layer.
